title: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-1 Art & Culture PART-4

questions.question: Kalbelia dance is generally performed in which of the following states of India?
questions.solution:
Kalbelia is a famous folk dance of Rajasthan, performed by the tribe of the same name. It is often called the 'Snake Charmer Dance' because the movements and costumes resemble those of a cobra.

Note: It was included in the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2010. Dancers wear traditional black skirts with heavy embroidery and dance to the tunes of the Been.

questions.question: Which of the following dances is NOT predominantly performed in the Indian state of Odisha?
questions.solution:
Bhavai is a folk dance predominantly performed in Gujarat and Rajasthan, not Odisha. It involves women balancing several earthen pots on their heads while dancing.
  • Paika: A martial folk dance of Odisha.
  • Ghumra: An ancient drum-based dance of Odisha.
  • Dhap: A folk dance from Western Odisha.

questions.question: The Raigarh Gharana is associated with which of the following dance forms?
questions.solution:
The Raigarh Gharana is a unique school of Kathak established by Raja Chakradhar Singh of Raigarh (Chhattisgarh). It is known for its blend of different styles from the Lucknow and Jaipur gharanas, with a heavy emphasis on percussion and Ganesh Paran.

Key Fact: Unlike other gharanas, it was developed under the direct patronage of a King who was himself a percussionist and dancer.

questions.question: Jamda folk dance is associated with which Indian state?
questions.solution:
Jamda is a folk dance associated with the state of Jharkhand. It is part of the rich tribal heritage of the region, often performed during seasonal festivals or community gatherings.

Additional Info: Jharkhand's folk culture is deeply tied to nature and agriculture, featuring other prominent dances like Chhau and Santhali.

questions.question: Who among the following was a Padma Bhushan awardee, legendary Bharatanatyam exponent, theosophist and founder of the Kalakshetra Dance School?
questions.solution:
Rukmini Devi Arundale was a legendary Bharatanatyam exponent and a theosophist. She is credited with the global revival of Bharatanatyam and founded the Kalakshetra school in Chennai to preserve the purity of the art form.

Recognition: She was the first woman in Indian history to be nominated as a member of the Rajya Sabha.

questions.question: Who among the following Kathak dancers of India founded the KADAMB Centre for Dance in 1964?
questions.solution:
Kumudini Lakhia is a renowned Kathak dancer and choreographer who founded the KADAMB Centre for Dance in Ahmedabad in 1964. She is a pioneer in modernizing Kathak choreography by moving away from solo storytelling to innovative group compositions.

Impact: Her work has been instrumental in changing the visual aesthetic of Kathak on the global stage.

questions.question: Giddha and Bhagra are the folk dances of which Indian state?
questions.solution:
Giddha and Bhangra are the iconic folk dances of Punjab.
  • Bhangra: Traditionally performed by men during the harvest festival of Baisakhi.
  • Giddha: A graceful and energetic dance performed by women, accompanied by Boliyan (folk singing) and clapping.

questions.question: Who was given the title of ‘Hanjaba’ by the Maharaj of Manipur for reviving Manipuri dance?
questions.solution:
Guru Bipin Singh was a master of Manipuri dance and was awarded the title of 'Hanjaba' by the Maharaja of Manipur for his exceptional efforts in reviving and systemizing the dance form.

Note: He combined traditional temple dance elements with modern stage techniques to make Manipuri dance popular worldwide.

questions.question: ‘Kalasam’ is a dance sequence in which of the following classical dances of India?
questions.solution:
A Kalasam is a distinctive dance sequence or a rhythmic conclusion in Kathakali. It is a pure dance piece (Nritta) that usually follows a verse or a dialogue to provide a transition or a dramatic flourish.

Technique: It involves vigorous footwork and body movements that showcase the physical prowess of the Kathakali performer.

questions.question: Which of the following personalities is a famous Bharatanatyam dancer?
questions.solution:
Padma Subrahmanyam is a globally recognized Bharatanatyam dancer, scholar, and choreographer. She is famous for her research into the Natya Shastra and for developing a style known as Bharatanatyam, which incorporates the 108 Karanas (temple sculptures' poses).

Note: Other mentioned artists like Birju Maharaj and Saswati Sen are maestros of Kathak.

questions.question: Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan awardee, Yamini Krishnamurthy is renowned for Bharatanatyam and which of the following dances?
questions.solution:
Yamini Krishnamurthy is an eminent classical dancer who is a master of both Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi. She has played a significant role in popularizing Kuchipudi as a solo classical dance form outside of Andhra Pradesh.

Honors: She has been honored with the Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Vibhushan.

questions.question: How many main styles of Chhau folk dance exist?
questions.solution:

questions.question: Dhalo is a folk dance of which Indian state?
questions.solution:
Dhalo is one of the most popular folk dances of Goa. It is a slow, graceful dance performed by women in the rural areas during the winter months (Pausha month).

Significance: It is performed for the protection of the household and to celebrate the bond between women and nature.

questions.question: Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan and Padma Vibushan awardee, Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra, was instrumental in reviving which of the following classical dances?
questions.solution:
Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra was a legendary guru and dancer who was the primary architect of the modern Odissi revival. He spent his life researching ancient sculptures and palm-leaf manuscripts to reconstruct the dance form after it had nearly disappeared.

Note: He was the first person from Odisha to be awarded the Padma Vibhushan.

questions.question: The Jagannath Temple in Puri depicts which Indian classical dance form?
questions.solution:
The Jagannath Temple in Puri is deeply connected to Odissi dance. Historically, the dance was performed within the temple complex by Maharis (temple dancers) as a ritual service to Lord Jagannath.

Visual Evidence: The stone carvings on the temple walls, particularly the Nata Mandapa (dancing hall), depict various Odissi poses and mudras.

questions.question: Raut Nacha is famous in which of these states?
questions.solution:
Raut Nacha is a traditional folk dance performed by the Yadav/Raut community of Chhattisgarh. It is performed during the Dev Uthani Ekadashi (after Diwali) and depicts the mock battles and celebrations of the cowherd community.

Theme: It primarily celebrates the victory of Lord Krishna over the demon King Kansa.

questions.question: Who among the following performing artists bagged the best actress award for Meena Gurjari in 1975?
questions.solution:
Mallika Sarabhai, a world-renowned dancer and actress, received the Best Actress award from the Government of Gujarat for the film Meena Gurjari in 1975.

Background: She is the daughter of the famous dancer Mrinalini Sarabhai and scientist Vikram Sarabhai, and she is an expert in both Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi.

questions.question: Who among the following musicians is popular for his mastery over the musical instrument Sitar?
questions.solution:
Vilayat Khan was one of the greatest Sitar maestros of the 20th century. He belonged to the Imdadkhani Gharana (Etawah Gharana) and was known for developing a style that mimicked the human voice, called Gayaki Ang.

Comparison: Amjad Ali Khan and Ali Akbar Khan are famous Sarod players.

questions.question: U Srinivas is a famous player of which of the following instruments?
questions.solution:
U. Srinivas (often called Mandolin Srinivas) was a child prodigy who brought the Mandolin, a Western instrument, into the world of Indian Carnatic Classical Music.

Legacy: He was known for his incredible speed and precision, and he was awarded the Padma Shri at a very young age.

questions.question: Pandit Kishan Maharaj of Benaras Gharana was a _______ player.
questions.solution:
Pandit Kishan Maharaj was a legendary Tabla player of the Benaras Gharana. He was known for his powerful 'Baaj' (style) and his ability to play with a wide variety of instrumentalists and vocalists.

Note: He was a recipient of the Padma Vibhushan and was a dominant figure in the 20th-century Indian percussion scene.

questions.question: Which of the following sitar players was awarded the Bharat Ratna in the year 1999?
questions.solution:
Pandit Ravi Shankar was awarded India's highest civilian honor, the Bharat Ratna, in 1999. He was a Sitar virtuoso who became the most famous Indian musician globally, collaborating with artists like The Beatles.

Additional Fact: He was also a composer and served as a member of the Rajya Sabha.

questions.question: Which of the following musical instruments were played by the musicians such as Shakoor Khan and Pandit Ram Narayan?
questions.solution:
Shakoor Khan and Pandit Ram Narayan were maestros of the Sarangi. Pandit Ram Narayan is particularly credited with bringing the Sarangi into the spotlight as a solo concert instrument, rather than just an accompanying instrument for vocalists.

Instrument Note: The Sarangi is a bowed, multi-stringed instrument known for its soulful, vocal-like sound.

questions.question: Which of the given personalities is NOT associated with Carnatic Music?
questions.solution:
Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande was a scholar of Hindustani Classical Music (North Indian), not Carnatic Music. He is famous for writing the first modern treatise on Hindustani music and for creating the Thaat system of classification.

Note: MS Subbulakshmi and Subramania Bharathiyar are icons of the Carnatic/South Indian tradition.

questions.question: Asad Ali Khan is best known for his mastery over which of the given musical instruments?
questions.solution:
Asad Ali Khan was one of the last great masters of the Rudra Veena. He belonged to the Khandarvani style of the Dhrupad tradition.

Instrument Fact: The Rudra Veena is a large plucked string instrument with two large resonators made of gourds, and it is rarely played today.

questions.question: hich of the following pairs of musicians and their instruments is INCORRECT?
questions.solution:
The pair Pt. Ram Narayan – Sarod is incorrect because Pandit Ram Narayan is a world-famous Sarangi player.
  • Corrected: Pt. Ram Narayan – Sarangi.
  • Pt. Ravi Shankar: Sitar (Correct).
  • N. Rajam: Violin (Correct).
  • Bismillah Khan: Shehnai (Correct).
